introduction_markdown: CAMEROON GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0520 COMMERCE 1, JUNE 2019, ORDINARY LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, one and a half hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination. Calculators are allowed. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; you can come back to it later. Do all rough work in the booklet using the blank spaces in the question booklet.

Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 6, 25, 38, 46. 6 : l'air et la mer sont tous deux des voies naturelles (clé visée d). 25 : les quatre options sont des moyens de règlement, un chèque barré reste un chèque (clé visée d). 38 : les options a et d disent la même chose (clé visée d). 46 : factor, broker, auctioneer et del credere sont tous payés à la commission (clé visée a).

questions.enonce_markdown: Commerce is usually sub-divided into:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Commerce is the part of business that moves goods from the producer to the consumer. It is divided into two branches: **trade** (buying and selling, that is wholesale, retail, home trade and foreign trade) and **aids to trade** (the services that help trade to take place: banking, insurance, transport, warehousing, communication and advertising). Option A names only one aid to trade (banking), option B only describes trade, and option C describes the whole chain of production and distribution, not the two branches of commerce.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the accounts below earns interest?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **deposit account** (savings or time deposit) is opened to keep money for some time, and the bank pays the holder interest for it. A current account is used for daily payments by cheque and normally earns no interest (the holder may even pay bank charges). 'Sight deposit' describes money that can be withdrawn on demand, like a current account, and 'loan deposit account' is not a standard type of account.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The term "Uberrimae Fidei" means:
questions.corrige_markdown:
*Uberrimae fidei* is a Latin phrase meaning **utmost good faith**. It is a basic principle of insurance: the proposer must disclose every material fact honestly when taking out the policy, and the insurer must also deal honestly. Indemnity (restoring the insured to the position before the loss), proximate cause (the nearest effective cause of the loss) and insurable interest (a financial interest in the thing insured) are other principles of insurance, with different meanings.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are banking institutions EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
BICEC is a commercial bank, BEAC is the central bank of the CEMAC zone, and NFC (National Financial Credit) is read in this question as a financial credit institution. **COBAC** (the Central African Banking Commission) is a supervisory body: it controls and regulates banks and credit institutions but does not itself provide banking services to the public. It is therefore the odd one out.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The price quotation which indicates that the cost of goods includes delivery charges is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
With **carriage paid** the seller pays the cost of delivering the goods, so the price quoted already includes the delivery charges. With *carriage forward* the buyer pays the delivery charges on arrival. *Cash on delivery* and *cash with order* are terms of payment (when the buyer pays), not terms about who pays for transport.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A transport mode that requires no special routes is called:

*Options as printed:* A) Road.   B) Rail.   C) Sea.   D) Air.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Road transport needs roads and rail transport needs tracks, and both must be built and maintained. Air transport uses the sky, so no route has to be constructed (only airports at the two ends), and the usual textbook answer is **air**. Note that sea transport also uses a natural waterway, so the question is not fully precise.

**Intended answer: D (Air).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: When profits are expressed as a percentage of cost price, this is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Mark-up** is the gross profit expressed as a percentage of the *cost price*: $\text{mark-up} = \dfrac{\text{gross profit}}{\text{cost price}} \times 100$. **Margin** is the gross profit expressed as a percentage of the *selling price*. Stock-turn (rate of turnover) and average stock concern the movement of stock, not profit.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An agent that earns extra income for guaranteeing payments for goods sold on credit is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **del credere agent** sells goods on credit for the principal and, in return for an extra commission, guarantees that the customers will pay. If a customer fails to pay, the agent bears the loss. A factor holds and sells goods for the principal, a broker only brings buyer and seller together, and a forwarding agent arranges the shipment of goods.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A cheque presented for payment after its expiration date is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A cheque is normally valid for six months. One presented to the bank after this period is a **stale cheque** and the bank will refuse to pay it. A *dishonoured* cheque is one the bank refuses to pay for any reason (for example lack of funds), a *post-dated* cheque carries a future date, and a *counter cheque* is a cheque form issued by the bank for use at its counter.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A public company issues which of the following documents when offering shares for sale?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A public company invites the public to buy its shares by issuing a **prospectus**, which gives the details of the company and of the share offer. The Memorandum and the Articles of Association are the documents that define the company and its internal rules, and the certificate of incorporation is the document that proves the company has been legally registered. None of these three is an invitation to the public to buy shares.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Enterprises can be classified according to the following EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Enterprises are classified by **ownership** (private, public, mixed), by **nature of activity** (primary, secondary, tertiary), and by **size** (small, medium, large). 'Responsibility' is not one of the usual bases of classification, so it is the exception.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: If stock at start is 10,000,000 CFAF, stock at close is 8,000,000 CFAF and cost of goods sold is 27,000,000 CFAF, calculate the rate of turnover:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Average stock $= \dfrac{10\,000\,000 + 8\,000\,000}{2} = 9\,000\,000$ CFAF.

Rate of turnover $= \dfrac{\text{cost of goods sold}}{\text{average stock}} = \dfrac{27\,000\,000}{9\,000\,000} = 3$ times.

The common error is to divide by the opening stock only (2.7 times) or by the closing stock (3.375 times).

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A warehouse where goods are kept pending payment of duties is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Imported goods on which customs duty has not yet been paid are stored in a **bonded warehouse**, under the control of the customs authorities. The duty is paid only when the goods are taken out for sale in the home market (or they may be re-exported free of duty). A public warehouse is open to any trader who pays rent, and a general warehouse stores a mixture of goods; neither is linked to the payment of duty.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A promotional tool used to boost the image of an atrophic [sic] is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The word 'atrophic' is a misprint in the paper (the intended word is most likely 'organisation'). The promotional tool whose aim is to build and protect the good image of an organisation is **public relations** (sponsoring events, press releases, open days). Advertisement and sales promotion aim to increase sales, and personal selling is face-to-face selling by a salesperson.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The charges for a Business Reply Service are paid by the:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the Business Reply Service a business sends out reply-paid cards or envelopes to its customers. The customers post them without a stamp, and the postal service collects the postage from the **business** (the seller) when the replies arrive. This encourages customers to answer.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An agreement for the hiring of ships is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **charter party** is the contract by which a shipowner hires out a ship (or part of it) to a merchant for a voyage or a period of time. 'Affreightment' is the general term for a contract to carry goods by ship, but the document for hiring a ship is the charter party. 'Contract policy' and 'assignment' have no such meaning here.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An insurance policy that is compulsory in Cameroon is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Motor vehicle owners must insure against **third party** risks, that is, injury or damage they may cause to other people, which protects the victims of road accidents. A comprehensive motor policy is wider (it also covers the owner's own vehicle) but is not compulsory, and fidelity guarantee and employer's liability are not the policy the question has in mind.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A bank account that enables the holder to obtain an overdraft facility is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
An overdraft lets the holder draw out more money than the balance on the account, up to an agreed limit. The bank allows it only on a **current account**, the account used for daily cheque payments. Savings, deposit and time deposit accounts are meant for keeping money and cannot be overdrawn.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The government department that controls the quality of meat and animal products is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Meat and animal products are inspected for health and quality by the **sanitation and veterinary department**, which protects consumers from unfit food. The price control department watches prices, the forestry department deals with forests and wildlife, and National Security is the police.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following investors below is a creditor to a company?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **debenture** is a loan to the company: the debenture holder lends money, is a creditor, and receives fixed interest whether or not the company makes a profit. Shareholders (ordinary, preference or cumulative preference) are part-owners of the company and receive dividends only from profit.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The factor of production that earns wages is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Each factor of production earns its own reward: land earns rent, capital earns interest, **labour** earns wages and the entrepreneur earns profit.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Impulse buying occurs when goods are purchased:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Impulse buying is a sudden decision to buy something that the customer had **not planned** to buy, often caused by attractive displays, advertisements or special offers near the till. Buying in bulk, on credit or at a discount describes the quantity or the terms of the purchase, not the lack of planning.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: "Net 30 days" on an invoice implies that:
questions.corrige_markdown:
'Net 30 days' means that the full (net) amount of the invoice must be paid within 30 days of the invoice date. A cash discount is an inducement for early payment, so it is **not allowed after the period has passed**. Trade discount is already deducted on the invoice and does not depend on the date of payment.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Trade discount is allowed within 30 days.
Cash discount is allowed on the 30th day.
Cash discount is not allowed after 30 days.

questions.enonce_markdown: The activity that ensures the storage of goods before sales is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The question asks for an *activity*. **Warehousing** is the activity of storing goods safely until they are needed by customers. A warehouse (and a bonded warehouse) is the building where the activity takes place, and advertising is unrelated to storage.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The methods below are used in settling commercial debts EXCEPT:

*Options as printed:* A) Money order.   B) Postal order.   C) Postal cheques.   D) Crossed cheques.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Money orders, postal orders and postal cheques are separate instruments used to send money and settle debts through the post office. A crossing, on the other hand, is only a safety instruction written on a cheque (two parallel lines) which makes the money payable into a bank account and not in cash; it is a protection of the cheque, not a separate method of settlement. The printed question is weak, because a crossed cheque is still a cheque and a cheque is a method of settling debts.

**Intended answer: D (Crossed cheques).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following risks is uninsurable?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A risk is insurable if the loss can be measured in money, the insured has an insurable interest, and the chance of loss can be estimated from past experience. Embezzlement by a cashier (fidelity guarantee), motor accidents and floods can all be insured. A **poor harvest** is treated as an uninsurable business risk in the textbook list, because it depends on many uncontrollable factors (weather, pests, market) and cannot be measured with enough accuracy.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The main role of an insurance company is to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
An insurance company collects small premiums from a large number of people who face the same kind of risk. The premiums are put together in a common fund from which the few who suffer a loss are compensated. The central idea, on which paying claims and covering risks depend, is the **pooling of risks**.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Charges paid by a ship for exceeding delay days is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Demurrage** is the compensation paid to the shipowner when the ship is kept at the port beyond the agreed days for loading or unloading. *Dead freight* is paid for space booked but not used, *freight* is the normal charge for carrying the goods, and *dock dues* are port charges for using the dock.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A complete prohibition on trade in goods is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
An **embargo** is a government ban on trading, completely, in certain goods or with a certain country. A quota only limits the quantity, a tariff is a tax on imports, and exchange control limits the use of foreign currency.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A credit note is identified easily because it is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A credit note is issued by the seller to reduce the amount owed by the buyer (goods returned, damaged goods or an overcharge on the invoice). To distinguish it from an invoice it is **usually printed in red**. Option B is wrong because an undercharge is corrected with a debit note, and options C and D confuse it with a cash or credit sale.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Used when goods are bought on credit.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Act that protects consumers against misleading adverts is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A Trade Descriptions Act makes it an offence to describe goods or services falsely or in a misleading way, including in advertisements. The Hire Purchase Act deals with credit sales, the Sale of Goods Act deals with the quality and description of goods sold, and 'quality control department' is a department, not an Act.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Owners of a joint stock company are called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The real owners of a joint stock company are its **ordinary shareholders**: they carry the risk, vote at general meetings and share in the profit. Preference shareholders have priority but a fixed dividend, and debenture holders are creditors, not owners.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An INCOTERM which covers the costs, freight and insurance on imports is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Of the four, only **CIP** (Carriage and Insurance Paid to) includes both the carriage and the insurance in the seller's price. C & F (cost and freight) has no insurance, FOB (free on board) ends at the loading of the goods on the ship, and DDP (delivered duty paid) includes everything up to the buyer's door, including duties, which is more than the question asks.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A manufacturer sells directly to consumers when:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Goods that are **perishable** (fresh bread, fish, milk) must reach the consumer quickly, so the producer cuts out the middlemen. The other statements are advantages the manufacturer may enjoy, but they are not the circumstance that forces direct selling.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: They want to make more profits.
Their location is nearer to consumers.
Transport costs need to be eliminated.

questions.enonce_markdown: In which circumstance may a debit note be used?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **debit note** is sent by the seller to the buyer to increase the amount owed, for example when the invoice was undercharged or a charge was left out. The other cases (goods returned, an overcharged invoice) are corrected with a credit note, and prompt payment earns a cash discount.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A polite request for payments before delivery of goods is effected by issuing:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **pro forma invoice** looks like an invoice but is not a demand for payment in the accounts. The seller sends it before the goods are delivered, so that the buyer pays in advance (and, for foreign trade, to obtain an import licence). A delivery note travels with the goods, an invoice is sent when the goods are supplied, and a credit note reduces a debt.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The choice of a good transport system will depend on all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A trader chooses a means of transport according to the cost (freight charges), the speed needed (urgency), and the quantity and weight of the goods (tonnage), as well as their nature and the distance. Weather is not one of the usual factors listed in the textbook and is the **exception** here, although bad weather can occasionally delay a particular journey.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Visible exports refers to:

*Options as printed:* A) Selling goods abroad.   B) Services sold abroad.   C) Goods bought from abroad.   D) Goods sold abroad.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Visible exports are the **tangible goods that a country sells to other countries** (cocoa, coffee, timber). Services sold abroad (tourism, insurance, banking) are invisible exports, and goods bought from abroad are visible imports. Options A and D say almost the same thing, so the printed question is not reliable.

**Intended answer: D (Goods sold abroad).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The production of goods for personal consumption implies:
questions.corrige_markdown:
When people produce goods for their own use (a farmer growing food for his own family), the production is **direct production**. Indirect production is production for sale or exchange. Primary and secondary production describe the stage of production (extraction, manufacturing), not who consumes the output.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that the cost of goods sold is 2,400,000 CFAF on a mark-up of 20%. Determine the gross profit.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Mark-up is a percentage of the cost price, so:

Gross profit $= 20\% \times 2\,400\,000 = \dfrac{20}{100} \times 2\,400\,000 = 480\,000$ CFAF.

(The selling price is then $2\,400\,000 + 480\,000 = 2\,880\,000$ CFAF.) The wrong options come from misplacing a zero.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An agent responsible for the shipment of goods is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **forwarding agent** arranges for goods to be transported: he books space on a ship, plane or lorry, prepares the shipping documents and deals with customs. A mercantile agent acts for a principal in selling or buying goods in general, a broker brings buyers and sellers together, and a factor sells goods held for the principal.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The offer of gifts and free samples to stimulate sales is referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Sales promotion** is made up of short-term inducements to buy such as free samples, gifts, discounts, coupons and competitions. Advertisement is a paid message in the media, publicity is unpaid mention in the media, and public relations builds the image of the organisation.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A trade restriction which is aimed at raising revenue is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **tariff** (customs duty) is a tax on imported goods and brings money to the government as well as protecting local industry. An export subsidy and a customs drawback give money back to exporters, and exchange control limits the use of foreign currency; none of them raises revenue.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A document prepared by a supplier showing the current prices and the terms of trade is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **price current** (price list) is a document issued by the supplier listing the current prices of the goods and the terms of trade (discounts, delivery, payment). A quotation is the answer to a particular enquiry for specific goods, an order form is filled in by the buyer, and a catalogue describes and illustrates the goods, usually with the prices separate. The question is close between A and B, so the key follows the wording 'current prices'.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Profit expressed as a percentage of cost price is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Mark-up** $= \dfrac{\text{gross profit}}{\text{cost price}} \times 100$. Margin uses the selling price as the base, and stock-turn and average stock are measures of stock movement.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
An agent who is paid a commission on goods sold is:

*Options as printed:* A) Factor.   B) Broker.   C) Auctioneer.   D) Del credere.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **factor** is an agent who holds the goods of the principal, sells them in his own name and is paid a commission on the goods sold. A broker is also paid a commission (brokerage) but does not hold the goods, an auctioneer is paid a commission on sales at an auction, and a del credere agent receives an extra commission for guaranteeing payment. Since all four are paid on a commission basis, the printed question is not precise.

**Intended answer: A (Factor).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A cheque that cannot be cashed before its due date is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **post-dated cheque** carries a date in the future, so the bank will not pay it before that date. A stale cheque is too old, a dishonoured cheque has been refused, and a crossed cheque can only be paid into a bank account.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Orders to buy items needed by any department in an enterprise are addressed to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Departments send a purchase requisition to the **purchase department**, which is the department that deals with suppliers, sends enquiries, compares quotations and places the orders. The stores department keeps the goods, the production department makes them, and the accounting department records and pays.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Production can be sub-divided into the following:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the textbook classification, the production of wealth is divided into **industry** (extraction, manufacturing, construction), **commerce** (trade and aids to trade) and **direct services** (the services of doctors, teachers, lawyers and so on). Option A repeats the same idea twice (trade is part of commerce), option B leaves out direct services and option C mixes branches of different levels.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A cheque guaranteed by a bank for payments is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **certified cheque** has been marked by the bank to confirm that the drawer has enough money in the account and that the amount has been set aside, so payment is guaranteed. A counter cheque is a bank form for withdrawals at the counter, a bearer cheque is payable to whoever holds it, and a post-dated cheque has a future date.

**Answer: D.**
